newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Maize up, wheat down in sleepy Budapest market.
newsitem.headline: Maize up, wheat down in sleepy Budapest market.

text.p: Grains futures prices moved mixed on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) in very light turnover, traders said on Monday.
"It was a mix of post-holiday lack of interest and wait-and-see attitude," said Robert Vajo of Termin.
Total grains turnover was an insignificant 110.6 million forints or 223 contracts, down from last Wednesday's 1,206 contracts or 563.45 million forints.
Milling wheat accounted for 156 lots of the total turnover with August easing 30 forints per tonne to 24,650, October down 250 to 25,600 and December down 300 to 26,700 forints.
Feed wheat prices went limit-down (400 forints) for August, October and December while September finished 390 forints lower.
Maize rose 100 forints for July to 18,900, October went up 400 to 19,800 and November rose 80 forints to 20,200.
Traders said they expected turnover to pick up towards the end of May as crop estimates would give new information to trade on.
